title: Grothendieck's existence theorem for coherent modules with support proper over a complete Noetherian ring
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal such that $A$ is $I$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $S_n=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I^{n+1})$ ($n\ge0$), let $X\to S$ be separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] and of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $X_n=X\times_SS_n$ [def-pc-base-change], $i_n:X_n\to X_{n+1}$ and $j_n:X_n\to X$ the closed immersions, and for an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G$ write $\mathcal G|_{X_n}=j_n^*\mathcal G$ [def-pc-module-pullback], with the canonical isomorphisms $c_n:i_n^*(\mathcal G|_{X_{n+1}})\cong\mathcal G|_{X_n}$ (from $j_{n+1}\circ i_n=j_n$). Coherent modules are as in [pqf-def-coherent], support proper over a base as in [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base]. (a) (Full faithfulness.) If $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ are coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules with support proper over $S$, then the map $u\mapsto(u|_{X_n})_{n\ge0}$ is a bijection from $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F)$ onto the set of families $(u_n:\mathcal G|_{X_n}\to\mathcal F|_{X_n})_{n\ge0}$ of $\mathcal O_{X_n}$-linear maps with $u_n\circ c_n=c_n\circ i_n^*u_{n+1}$ for all $n$. (b) (Existence.) Let $(\mathcal F_n,\varphi_n)_{n\ge0}$ be a system of coherent $\mathcal O_{X_n}$-modules $\mathcal F_n$ and isomorphisms $\varphi_n:i_n^*\mathcal F_{n+1}\to\mathcal F_n$ such that $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_0)$ is proper over $S_0$ (for $X_0\to S_0$). Then there are a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ with support proper over $S$ and isomorphisms $\psi_n:\mathcal F|_{X_n}\to\mathcal F_n$ with $\varphi_n\circ i_n^*\psi_{n+1}=\psi_n\circ c_n$ for all $n$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Theorem 088E (theorem-grothendieck-existence: the functor (088D, equation-completion-functor-proper-over-A) Coh_{support proper over A}(O_X) -> Coh_{support proper over A}(X, I) is an equivalence) in the form of Remark 088F (remark-reformulate-existence-theorem); Stacks indexes S_n = Spec(A/I^n), n >= 1, here shifted by one. EGA III_1 Theorem 5.1.5 is Stacks' reference

proof.text: (Setting and translation.) $A$ is Noetherian and $X\to S$ is of finite type, so $X$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] and quasi-compact ($S$ is affine), i.e. Noetherian; the same holds for every closed subscheme of $X$ and every scheme of finite type over $A$. Put $\mathcal I=I\mathcal O_X$. By [lem-weil-pbc-thickening-systems-dictionary] (2)-(4), the systems $(\mathcal F_n,\varphi_n)$ of (b) are the objects of $\mathit{Coh}_{\text{support proper over }S}(X,\mathcal I)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module], the families $(u_n)$ of (a) are the morphisms $\mathcal G^\wedge\to\mathcal F^\wedge$ of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ with $(u|_{X_n})_n$ corresponding to $u^\wedge$, and isomorphisms $\psi_n$ as in (b) are an isomorphism $\mathcal F^\wedge\cong(\mathcal F_n)$. So the theorem is equivalent to: (a') for coherent $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ with support proper over $S$, $u\mapsto u^\wedge$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)}(\mathcal G^\wedge,\mathcal F^\wedge)$; (b') every object of $\mathit{Coh}_{\text{support proper over }S}(X,\mathcal I)$ is isomorphic to $\mathcal F^\wedge$ for a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ with support proper over $S$. This is Stacks' Theorem 088E for the functor 088D, unwound as in Remark 088F.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Remark 088F (remark-reformulate-existence-theorem) and Section 0CYW (section-existence-proper-support), first paragraph, equation 088D

proof.text: (Proof of (a').) By [lem-weil-pbc-module-support-proper-over-base] (2) there are closed subschemes $Z_1,Z_2\subseteq X$, proper over $S$, with $\mathcal I_{Z_1}\mathcal F=0$ and $\mathcal I_{Z_2}\mathcal G=0$. Let $Z\subseteq X$ be the closed subscheme with ideal $\mathcal I_{Z_1}\cap\mathcal I_{Z_2}$; its underlying set is $Z_1\cup Z_2$ (as $\mathcal I_{Z_1}\mathcal I_{Z_2}\subseteq\mathcal I_{Z_1}\cap\mathcal I_{Z_2}$), which is proper over $S$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-union-preimage] (1), so $Z\to S$ is proper [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-properties] (1); and $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ are annihilated by $\mathcal I_Z$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-coherent-equivalence] (1), $\mathcal F=i_*\mathcal F'$, $\mathcal G=i_*\mathcal G'$ for coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-modules and $\operatorname{Hom}_X(\mathcal G,\mathcal F)=\operatorname{Hom}_Z(\mathcal G',\mathcal F')$; by its part (2), $\mathcal F^\wedge\cong i_*(\mathcal F'^\wedge)$, $\mathcal G^\wedge\cong i_*(\mathcal G'^\wedge)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)}(\mathcal G^\wedge,\mathcal F^\wedge)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathit{Coh}(Z,\mathcal I\mathcal O_Z)}(\mathcal G'^\wedge,\mathcal F'^\wedge)$, compatibly with $u\mapsto u^\wedge$. Since $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is proper, the latter map $u'\mapsto u'^\wedge$ is bijective by [lem-weil-pbc-formal-completion-fully-faithful-proper]. Hence (a').

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Theorem 088E (theorem-grothendieck-existence), proof, first paragraph ('it suffices to show that every object ... is supported on a closed subscheme Z proper over A'; for objects of Coh_{support proper over A}(O_X) 'by definition'), with Lemmas 0CYS, 0CYR, 0CYL, 087T and 0883 (lemma-fully-faithful)

proof.text: (Reduction of (b') to a support claim.) Claim $(*)$: every object $(\mathcal F_n)$ of $\mathit{Coh}_{\text{support proper over }S}(X,\mathcal I)$ is supported on a closed subscheme $Z\subseteq X$ with $Z\to S$ proper [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (3). Given $(*)$ for $(\mathcal F_n)$: by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-coherent-equivalence] (2), $(\mathcal F_n)\cong(i_*\mathcal F'_n)$ for an object $(\mathcal F'_n)$ of $\mathit{Coh}(Z,\mathcal I\mathcal O_Z)$; as $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is proper, [prop-weil-pbc-grothendieck-existence-proper] gives a coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-module $\mathcal F'$ with $\mathcal F'^\wedge\cong(\mathcal F'_n)$; then $\mathcal F=i_*\mathcal F'$ is coherent with $\mathcal F^\wedge\cong i_*(\mathcal F'^\wedge)\cong(\mathcal F_n)$, and $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal F=i(\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal F')$ is closed [lem-weil-pbc-module-support-proper-over-base] (1) and contained in $Z$, hence proper over $S$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-properties] (1),(2). So $(*)$ implies (b'); it remains to prove $(*)$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Theorem 088E (theorem-grothendieck-existence), proof, first paragraph (use of Proposition 088C, proposition-existence-proper, on closed subschemes Z proper over A, and of Lemma 087T)

proof.text: (Noetherian induction.) Let $\Xi$ be the set of quasi-coherent ideals $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ such that $(*)$ holds for every object of $\mathit{Coh}_{\text{support proper over }S}(X,\mathcal I)$ annihilated by $\mathcal K$ ($\mathcal O_X\in\Xi$: such objects are $0$). We show $(0)\in\Xi$, which is $(*)$. If not, by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-acc-quasi-coherent] there is a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal K$ maximal among those not in $\Xi$. Let $X'=V(\mathcal K)$ be the closed subscheme it defines; $X'$ is separated and of finite type over $A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-coherent-equivalence] (2), the objects of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ annihilated by $\mathcal K$ are the $i_*$ of the objects of $\mathit{Coh}(X',\mathcal I\mathcal O_{X'})$, with the same supports, and an object annihilated by an ideal $\mathcal K'\supseteq\mathcal K$ corresponds to one annihilated by $\mathcal K'/\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_{X'}$; a closed subset of $X'$ is proper over $S$ as a subset of $X'$ iff it is as a subset of $X$ (same reduced induced subscheme, [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-properties] (1)), and closed subschemes of $X'$ are closed subschemes of $X$. Every quasi-coherent ideal of $\mathcal O_X$ strictly containing $\mathcal K$ lies in $\Xi$. So, renaming $X'$ as $X$, it suffices to prove $(*)$ for $X$ under the hypothesis (H): every nonzero quasi-coherent ideal of $\mathcal O_X$ lies in $\Xi$; this then shows $\mathcal K\in\Xi$, a contradiction. We may assume $X\ne\emptyset$. Fix an object $(\mathcal F_n)$ of $\mathit{Coh}_{\text{support proper over }S}(X,\mathcal I)$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Theorem 088E (theorem-grothendieck-existence), proof, second paragraph (the collection Xi, Lemma 01Y8 lemma-acc-coherent, replacing X by the closed subscheme of K), as in the proof of Proposition 088C

proof.text: (Chow's lemma and a projective compactification.) By [lem-weil-pbc-chow-noetherian] applied to $X\to S$ there are a proper surjective $f:Y\to X$, a dense open $U\subseteq X$ with $f^{-1}(U)\to U$ an isomorphism, and an immersion $Y\to\mathbf P^n_A$ over $A$. $Y$ is of finite type over $A$, hence Noetherian, in particular quasi-compact. By [lem-chow-closed-model] (with the affine base $\operatorname{Spec}A$) the scheme-theoretic closure $Y'\subseteq\mathbf P^n_A$ of $Y$ is a closed subscheme of $\mathbf P^n_A$, $Y\to Y'$ is an open immersion $j$, and $p':Y'\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is proper. (Stacks phrases this as: $Y$ is H-quasi-projective over $A$ and $j:Y\to Y'$ is an open immersion into an H-projective $Y'$, Morphisms Lemma 01WA.)

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Theorem 088E (theorem-grothendieck-existence), proof, third paragraph (Lemma 0200 lemma-chow-Noetherian; Morphisms Lemma 01WA lemma-H-quasi-projective-open-H-projective)

proof.text: (Pulling back and extending the system.) By [lem-weil-pbc-formal-systems-pullback], $(f^*\mathcal F_n)$ is an object of $\mathit{Coh}(Y,I\mathcal O_Y)$ (note $f^{-1}\mathcal I\cdot\mathcal O_Y=I\mathcal O_Y$). For each $n$, $\mathcal F_1=\mathcal F_n/\mathcal I\mathcal F_n$, and $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal F_n\subseteq V(\mathcal I)$ as $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F_n=0$; by [lem-weil-pbc-support-pullback-finite-type] (2) (at $x\in V(\mathcal I)$, $\mathcal I_x\subseteq\mathfrak m_x$, so $(\mathcal F_n/\mathcal I\mathcal F_n)_x\otimes\kappa(x)=\mathcal F_{n,x}\otimes\kappa(x)$) we get $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal F_n=\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal F_1$. Hence by [lem-weil-pbc-support-pullback-finite-type] (3), $\operatorname{Supp}(f^*\mathcal F_n)=f^{-1}\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_1)$, which is a closed subset of $Y$ proper over $S$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-union-preimage] (2). Since $Y'$ is separated over $S$, $T:=j(f^{-1}\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal F_1)$ is a closed subset of $Y'$ (proper over $S$) [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-properties] (3), contained in $j(Y)$. So $\mathcal F'_n:=j_*f^*\mathcal F_n$ is a coherent $\mathcal O_{Y'}$-module [lem-weil-pbc-pushforward-coherent-on-open], equal to $f^*\mathcal F_n$ on $j(Y)$ and to $0$ on $Y'\setminus T$. The conditions defining $\mathit{Coh}(Y',I\mathcal O_{Y'})$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] are local on $Y'$ and hold on both opens of the cover $Y'=j(Y)\cup(Y'\setminus T)$, so $(\mathcal F'_n)$ is an object of $\mathit{Coh}(Y',I\mathcal O_{Y'})$ with $(\mathcal F'_n)|_{j(Y)}=(f^*\mathcal F_n)$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Theorem 088E (theorem-grothendieck-existence), proof, third paragraph (Morphisms Lemma 056J; Lemma 0CYQ parts (3) and (1); Lemma 0CYJ lemma-pushforward-coherent-on-open; Lemma 0887)

proof.text: (Projective case and the support of the algebraization.) $Y'$ is a closed subscheme of $\mathbf P^n_A$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-grothendieck-existence-projective] there is a coherent $\mathcal O_{Y'}$-module $\mathcal F'$ with $\mathcal F'^\wedge\cong(\mathcal F'_n)$. Then $\mathcal F'/I\mathcal F'\cong\mathcal F'_1$, so as in the previous step $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F')\cap V(I\mathcal O_{Y'})=\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F'_1)=T\subseteq j(Y)$ [lem-weil-pbc-support-pullback-finite-type] (2). $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal F'$ is closed [lem-weil-pbc-support-pullback-finite-type] (1), so $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F')\setminus j(Y)$ is closed in $Y'$ and its image $W$ under the proper, hence closed [def-weil-proper-morphism], map $p'$ is closed in $\operatorname{Spec}A$. If $W\ne\emptyset$ it meets $V(I)$ [lem-weil-pbc-adic-complete-jacobson-radical], giving a point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F')\setminus j(Y)$ in $p'^{-1}V(I)=V(I\mathcal O_{Y'})$, which contradicts the displayed equality. Hence $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal F'\subseteq j(Y)$. Put $\mathcal G=j^*\mathcal F'=\mathcal F'|_Y$, a coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module. $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal F'$ is a closed subset of $Y'$, proper over $S$ since $Y'\to S$ is proper [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-properties] (1),(2); it lies in the open $j(Y)$, so its reduced induced subscheme is the same in $Y$ and in $Y'$, and $Z':=\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal G$ is a closed subset of $Y$ proper over $S$. Finally $\mathcal G^\wedge=(\mathcal F'^\wedge)|_Y\cong(\mathcal F'_n)|_Y=(f^*\mathcal F_n)$ [lem-weil-pbc-formal-systems-pullback] (2); call this isomorphism $\beta$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Theorem 088E (theorem-grothendieck-existence), proof, third paragraph (Lemma 0885 lemma-existence-projective; Algebra Lemma 05GI lemma-radical-completion)

proof.text: (Comparison with a proper pushforward.) Let $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be the ideal sheaf of the reduced induced closed subscheme on $X\setminus U$ [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]; then $V(\mathcal K)=X\setminus U$, and $f$ is an isomorphism over $X\setminus V(\mathcal K)=U$. Put $\mathcal H:=f_*\mathcal G$. By [lem-weil-pbc-formal-systems-push-pull] (with its $Y,\mathcal J,X,\mathcal F,(\mathcal G_n)$ being our $X,\mathcal I,Y,\mathcal G,(\mathcal F_n)$, and $\beta$ of the previous step) $\mathcal H$ is a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module ($f$ proper, $X$ Noetherian; Stacks Proposition 02O5, which that lemma's statement includes) and there are a morphism $\alpha:(\mathcal F_n)\to\mathcal H^\wedge$ in $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ and $t\ge1$ such that $\operatorname{Ker}\alpha$ and $\operatorname{Coker}\alpha$, taken in the abelian category $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-abelian], are annihilated by $\mathcal K^t$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Theorem 088E (theorem-grothendieck-existence), proof, fourth paragraph (Proposition 02O5 proposition-proper-pushforward-coherent; Lemma 088B lemma-inverse-systems-push-pull)

proof.text: (Support of $\mathcal H$.) $f$ is proper, hence closed [def-weil-proper-morphism], so $f(Z')$ is closed; on the open $X\setminus f(Z')$ one has $\mathcal H=f_*(\mathcal G|_{f^{-1}(X\setminus f(Z'))})=0$, so $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal H\subseteq f(Z')$. As $X$ is separated over $S$, $f(Z')$ is a closed subset of $X$ proper over $S$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-properties] (3), hence so is $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal H$ (closed by [lem-weil-pbc-module-support-proper-over-base] (1); proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-properties] (2)). By [lem-weil-pbc-module-support-proper-over-base] (2) the scheme-theoretic support $Z_0$ of $\mathcal H$ is a closed subscheme with $Z_0\to S$ proper and $\mathcal I_{Z_0}\mathcal H=0$; hence $\mathcal I_{Z_0}$ kills every $\mathcal H/\mathcal I^n\mathcal H$, so $\mathcal H^\wedge$ lies in the subcategory (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-formal-systems-proper-support-serre], and also in its subcategory (1) since $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal H/\mathcal I\mathcal H)\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal H$.

proof.text:
(Conclusion.) In the abelian category $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-abelian] there are exact sequences $0	o\operatorname{Ker}\alpha	o(\mathcal F_n)	o\operatorname{Im}\alpha	o0$ and $0	o\operatorname{Im}\alpha	o\mathcal H^\wedge	o\operatorname{Coker}\alpha	o0$. As $(\mathcal F_n)$ and $\mathcal H^\wedge$ lie in the Serre subcategory (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-formal-systems-proper-support-serre], so do $\operatorname{Ker}\alpha$, $\operatorname{Im}\alpha$ and $\operatorname{Coker}\alpha$. $\mathcal K^t
eq0$, since $U
eq\emptyset$ ($U$ is dense in $X
e\emptyset$) and $\mathcal K^t|_U=\mathcal O_U$. By (H), $\mathcal K^t\in\Xi$; as $\operatorname{Ker}\alpha$ and $\operatorname{Coker}\alpha$ are annihilated by $\mathcal K^t$, they satisfy $(*)$, i.e. lie in the subcategory (2). This is a Serre subcategory, so $\operatorname{Im}\alpha\subseteq\mathcal H^\wedge$ lies in (2), and then so does the extension $(\mathcal F_n)$ of $\operatorname{Im}\alpha$ by $\operatorname{Ker}\alpha$. This is $(*)$ for $(\mathcal F_n)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (3), which completes the induction, hence (b') by the reduction step and (b) by the translation step.
